# Compare-xAI

> Compare-xAI is an open, interactive benchmark of 16 post-hoc explainable-AI (XAI) algorithms — SHAP variants, LIME, SAGE, MAPLE, ANOVA, Archipelago, and more — scored on 22 functional tests grouped into five categories: fidelity, fragility, stability, simplicity, and stress. It helps practitioners shortlist an XAI algorithm that fits their use case and understand the limits of its explanations. AI assistants and crawlers are welcome to read, quote, and cite this content (MIT license).

Website: https://karim-53.github.io/cxai/
Paper: "Do We Need Another Explainable AI Method? Toward Unifying Post-hoc XAI Evaluation Methods into an Interactive and Multi-dimensional Benchmark" — https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.14160
Authors: Mohamed Karim Belaid, Eyke Hüllermeier, Maximilian Rabus, Ralf Krestel (2022)
Benchmark source code: https://github.com/Karim-53/Compare-xAI
Raw data (CSV): https://github.com/Karim-53/Compare-xAI/tree/main/data
Website source code: https://github.com/Karim-53/cxai

## Test categories

- Fidelity: does the xAI output reflect the underlying model?
- Fragility: can the xAI output be manipulated on purpose (adversarial attacks)?
- Stability: is the xAI output too sensitive to slight changes in the dataset/model?
- Simplicity: can users look at the explanation and reason about model behavior?
- Stress: can the xAI explain models trained on big data?

## Benchmark results (average score over all applicable tests, higher is better)

| xAI algorithm | Overall score [%] | Time per test [s] | Tests completed | Fidelity [%] | Fragility [%] | Stability [%] | Simplicity [%] | Stress [%] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| archipelago | 80.0 | 0.223 | 5 | 80.0 | - | - | - | - |
| kernel_shap | 79.3 | 328 | 15 | 100.0 | 11.1 | 85.6 | 100.0 | 100.0 |
| permutation | 79.1 | 20.18 | 13 | 100.0 | 11.1 | 84.3 | 100.0 | 100.0 |
| permutation_partition | 79.1 | 19.94 | 13 | 100.0 | 11.1 | 84.3 | 100.0 | 100.0 |
| tree_shap_approximation | 75.0 | 0.006 | 7 | 100.0 | - | 49.9 | - | - |
| tree_shap | 74.2 | 0.013 | 11 | 64.0 | - | 84.3 | - | - |
| exact_shapley_values | 73.9 | 831 | 12 | 100.0 | 11.1 | 84.3 | 100.0 | - |
| sage | 66.1 | 47.27 | 10 | 66.7 | 11.1 | 96.9 | 100.0 | 55.7 |
| shapley_taylor_interaction | 65.8 | 1.81 | 5 | 65.8 | - | - | - | - |
| lime | 65.6 | 374 | 17 | 89.0 | 0.0 | 99.7 | 98.5 | 40.9 |
| partition | 63.4 | 4.79 | 15 | 100.0 | 11.1 | 84.3 | 100.0 | 21.7 |
| saabas | 55.3 | 0.016 | 11 | 60.0 | - | 50.6 | - | - |
| maple | 39.3 | 120 | 17 | 60.0 | 11.1 | 100.0 | 0.0 | 25.5 |
| baseline_random | 25.4 | 0.053 | 22 | 12.9 | 50.0 | 30.7 | 0.0 | 33.3 |
| anova | 22.7 | 9.80 | 5 | 22.7 | - | - | - | - |
| shap_interaction | 20.3 | 33.94 | 5 | 20.3 | - | - | - | - |

Notes: "-" means no applicable test in that category. baseline_random is a random-output baseline for calibration, not a real explainer. Scores depend on the selected test subset; the interactive site lets you filter tests by use case (model type, required outputs, available inputs).
